## Tours visiting Atacama's Moon Valley: which itinerary to choose

[Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/) lies near [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). Here, among salt flats, dunes, and the ridges of the Cordillera de la Sal, visitors encounter desert almost entirely devoid of vegetation. Many come in the late afternoon to see the light on the rocks; the exact route and visiting hours depend on the itinerary and access rules.

The catalog brings together {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with this place on their main route. On some trips, Moon Valley is a key highlight of a short introduction to the Atacama. On others, it is the first northern stage of a journey that continues into Patagonia, Rapa Nui, or beyond Chile.

## A short trip to the north or several climate zones

[“Chile: An Otherworldly Journey on Earth”](/chile/tour/chile-otherworldly-journey/) lasts 6 days. After exploring Santiago and the Pacific coast, travelers fly north for a group excursion to Moon Valley and [Death Valley](/chile/place/death-valley-atacama/), with an emphasis on sunset. An astronomy excursion is listed separately as an optional activity, so it should not be treated as an obligatory part of the trip.

The [7-day tour through Santiago, the Atacama and Torres del Paine](/chile/tour/chile-santiago-atacama-torres-del-paine/) offers greater geographical contrasts. It includes a visit to Moon Valley after arrival in Calama, followed by a salt flat, high-altitude sites, and onward travel to Chilean Patagonia. The description of the specific day includes admission to the valley and a cocktail. Moving between regions makes this itinerary more intensive than a short trip focused solely on the north.

The [9-day “Chile's Hidden Treasures” tour](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) combines the Atacama, Patagonia, the Marble Caves, and glacial landscapes. The [12-day tour with Easter Island](/chile/tour/best-of-chile-easter-island-12-days/) adds the cultural heritage of Rapa Nui to the desert. These options are suitable if you want to see different sides of Chile and the interest in several regions justifies the flight time.

## When Moon Valley forms part of a larger journey

[“Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama”](/multi-country/tour/sun-tango-wine-atacama/) connects the natural landscapes of northern Chile with urban and culinary experiences in other South American countries. This combination has a different focus from a desert expedition: Moon Valley becomes one stop among varied parts of the itinerary.

[“VIP Chile 5*”](/chile/tour/chile-five-star-vip/) covers the Atacama, Patagonia, and the coast, while the [VIP tour featuring the Atacama and gastronomy](/chile/tour/chile-vip-atacama-patagonia-gourmet/) combines desert excursions with other activities. The word VIP in a title is not a substitute for comparing the actual conditions: check the specific hotels, guiding, transport, and included services for each tour.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_chili_kosmicheskoe_puteshestvie_na_zemle,tour_source_chili_santyago_pustynya_atakama_torres_del_pajne,tour_chile_hidden_secrets_9_days_2027,tour_source_chili_samoe_luchshee,tour_source_vip_chili_5}}

## Which other Atacama sites should you compare?

Moon Valley is a place for walking and observing geological formations. The [Atacama Salt Flat](/chile/place/atacama-salt-flat/) offers a very different experience: a wide salt plain and areas with lagoons. [Miscanti Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-miscanti/) provides high-altitude views, while the [El Tatio geysers](/chile/place/el-tatio-geysers/) require a separate early departure. Similar mentions of “Atacama” in tour titles therefore do not mean the itineraries are identical.

Compare the sequence of days first: are there overnight stays in San Pedro de Atacama, is there enough time for walks, and are the chosen trips to lagoons and geysers included? A Moon Valley visit is usually easy to combine with a stay in San Pedro, while more distant sites need different timing and preparation.

## Weather, altitude and transport

In the desert, intense sunshine comes with dry air and a marked drop in temperature in the evening. For Moon Valley, bring water, comfortable closed shoes, a hat, and sun protection. High-altitude lagoons and geysers require warmer clothing. These are different excursion conditions even if both outings depart from the same village.

International journeys usually pass through Santiago, while the northern stage uses Calama Airport followed by an overland transfer. Allow some flexibility for flight connections; visiting the valley on the arrival day depends on the actual timetable, transfer time, and last admission to the site. We can help coordinate the order of excursions with travel times and confirmed access hours.

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting Moon Valley

### Can I see Moon Valley at sunset?

Yes. Many itineraries choose the evening hours. For example, the [6-day itinerary](/chile/tour/chile-otherworldly-journey/) lists sunset as a main part of the excursion. Access to specific viewpoints and the last admission time must still be confirmed before travel.

### Does visiting Moon Valley mean an excursion to the geysers?

No. [El Tatio](/chile/place/el-tatio-geysers/) is in another part of the region and must appear separately on the itinerary. The same applies to lagoons and the salt flat.

### What should I choose for my first trip to Chile?

A short itinerary through San Pedro de Atacama is suitable for exploring the desert in depth. If you also want to see the glaciers and granite mountains of the south, compare [Chile tours](/chile/tour/) with flights to Patagonia.

### Is Moon Valley suitable without trekking experience?

Viewing the scenic areas does not usually require specialist athletic experience, but trail conditions, walking times, and weather vary. Travelers with limited mobility should check access to particular stops in advance.

## Milodón Cave: prehistoric Patagonia beneath an immense roof

**Milodón Cave** lies approximately **25 km north of Puerto Natales** in southern Chile. It is an enormous natural cavity known for finds of ancient skin and other remains of an extinct giant ground sloth. Visiting offers a glimpse of the natural world long before modern settlements.

The area is protected as **Monumento Natural Cueva del Milodón** and managed by Chile's National Forestry Corporation, CONAF.

## What was the milodón?

The milodón was a large mammal related to modern sloths. It lived in southern South America in prehistoric times and has long been extinct. Its history is connected to other ancient Patagonian animals and to changes in the region's climate.

According to Chile's Council of National Monuments, in **1895**, members of an expedition associated with Hermann Eberhard found an unusual fragment of skin with fur and bony inclusions in the cave. This material attracted researchers' attention and helped confirm the existence of large extinct fauna in the south of the continent.

Traces of ancient human activity and remains of other animals have also been studied within the monument. The site is therefore part of both natural and archaeological heritage.

## How did the cave form?

In ancient times, bodies of water near glaciers occupied this area. Waves and the erosion of rock gradually created a wide overhang and large cavity. Today, visitors see a vast entrance, an overhanging rock wall, and a space illuminated by daylight.

It is not a narrow underground labyrinth. Its main value lies in the geological monument itself, the history of the ancient landscape, and scientific discoveries.

## Which walking route should you choose?

The natural monument has official walking paths.

| Trail | Length |
|---|---|
| Cueva Grande | approximately 350 m |
| Cuevas y Aleros | approximately 4.3 km |

According to CONAF, the short approach to the main cave takes about **30 minutes**. The longer trail leads to additional caves and rock shelters and requires several hours. Sections may close temporarily for safety reasons, so check current access before traveling.

Do not leave permitted paths, damage rock surfaces, remove findings, or leave litter. These rules protect archaeological materials and the natural environment.

## The cave on the way to Torres del Paine

The cave is often visited during a journey from Puerto Natales to [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). This combination lets travelers see evidence of ancient animals as well as the park's present-day mountain landscapes. Depending on the program, the itinerary continues to lakes, including [Pehoé](/chile/place/lake-pehoe/).

If a long mountain trek is planned, treat a brief visit to the main cave and a several-hour walk among the additional shelters as separate options.

## Weather and visiting conditions

Southern Patagonia is known for sudden weather changes and strong winds. Even in summer, bring a windproof jacket, warm clothing, and shoes with reliable grip. Trails can have snow and ice in winter.

**CONAF and Pases Parques** publish opening hours, prices, and current rules. Old travel descriptions are no substitute for checking the present status of the trails.

## Frequently asked questions about Milodón Cave

### Does the milodón still live in the cave?

No. It is an extinct animal, and the cave is known for scientific discoveries of its remains.

### How long does a visit take?

The main short route takes about half an hour; other routes require several hours.

### How far is the cave from Puerto Natales?

Approximately 25 km north of the city.

### Can I combine it with Torres del Paine?

Yes. It is one of the natural stops on the way to the [national park](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), provided there is enough time for both parts of the journey.

## Which Patagonia tours include Milodón Cave?

[Milodón Cave](/chile/place/mylodon-cave/) lies approximately 25 km from [Puerto Natales and the Torres del Paine area](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). This protected natural monument has an immense rock overhang. Its name comes from the extinct giant ground sloth Mylodon darwini, whose remains researchers discovered here in the late 19th century.

This page brings together {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} visiting the site on their main route. The cave appears in different itineraries, but the length of the stop, number of days spent in the park, and logistics between Chile and Argentina vary. Choose based on the entire Patagonia section of the journey, not a single attraction.

## The cave as part of a Torres del Paine visit

On the [7-day Santiago–Atacama–Torres del Paine tour](/chile/tour/chile-santiago-atacama-torres-del-paine/), Patagonia follows the desert landscapes of the north. One day includes a visit to the cave and a drive through the national park. This itinerary suits travelers who want to experience the contrast between desert, lakes, and granite mountains within a limited overall time.

The [9-day “Chile's Hidden Treasures” itinerary](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) includes a full-day excursion with an early departure for the cave, followed by Torres del Paine. The specific program lists admission to both the park and cave, lunch, and a return to Puerto Natales. This makes a useful comparison with other routes: do not assume that included services are identical just because an excursion has the same name.

[“VIP Chile 5*”](/chile/tour/chile-five-star-vip/) combines the cave with Patagonian lakes and a trip to Grey Glacier. Compare its terms separately with regular itineraries: the word VIP does not automatically confirm a private excursion, a particular room category, or any specific package of services.

## When Argentina and Bolivia are added

[“Patagonian Expanses: Chile and Argentina”](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-chile-argentina-journey/) is an 8-day itinerary with the cave on its Chilean nature-focused leg. The wider choice depends on whether you want only Chilean scenery or are also interested in Argentina's glaciers and cities.

[“Chile & Argentina Deluxe”](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-deluxe/) combines the cave and Torres del Paine with other areas of both countries. [“Patagonia and the Uyuni Salt Flat”](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-uyuni-salt-flats-12-days/) extends the journey to Bolivia, allowing travelers to combine southern glaciers with high-altitude salt plains. This combination places greater demands on the pace and number of transfers; it does not make the trip “better” for every traveler.

[“Hidden Treasures of Bolivia and Chile”](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) also includes Milodón Cave within a long itinerary covering very different climatic regions. Warm clothing suited to both the highlands and Patagonia, along with sensible connections between stages, is especially important.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_chili_santyago_pustynya_atakama_torres_del_pajne,tour_chile_hidden_secrets_9_days_2027,tour_source_vip_chili_5,tour_source_prostory_patagonii_chili_i_argentina_v_odnom_puteshestvii,tour_source_prekrasnaya_patagoniya_i_solonchak_uyuni}}

## What you will see in the cave

The natural monument's main significance lies in the scale of the cavity and its archaeological heritage. The finds reveal ancient Patagonian animals and human presence in the area thousands of years ago. A model of the milodón helps visitors picture this extinct animal; of course, encountering a living milodón is impossible.

Exploring the cave and visiting [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) offer different experiences. The cave is interesting for its geology and history of research; the national park features mountain ranges, steppe, lakes, and glacier views. Much of the day may therefore be spent in the park, with the cave as one stop on the road.

Plan enough time for the walk from the entrance area and possible restrictions on sections of the trails. Chile's conservation authority CONAF publishes information on access and temporary closures. Before traveling, we check current conditions so the route does not rely on outdated assumptions about open paths.

## Choosing a season and preparing for the trip

Patagonian weather is changeable even during the warmer months: wind, rain, and cold may alternate within a single day. Walks call for a windproof jacket, footwear with reliable grip, and rain protection. It is better not to schedule every minute too rigidly when exploring natural sites, especially if the route includes lakes and remote viewpoints.

Puerto Natales is usually the base for excursions. If a tour combines Chile and Argentina, take account of the border crossing and different arrival and departure airports. Adding Bolivia also brings changes in altitude and climate. We can help coordinate the sequence of overland stages and match the pace to your group's needs.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Milodón Cave

### Is it the same excursion as visiting Torres del Paine?

No. The cave is a separate natural monument, while [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) is a large national park. Some tours combine them into one full day, but admission arrangements and tickets differ.

### Is cave admission included in every tour?

There is no universal rule. For example, the [9-day tour](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) explicitly lists the ticket. For another route, check its own “Included” section.

### Is there a real milodón skeleton here?

The monument is known for paleontological finds of milodón and other ancient animals, but a tourist visit should not be confused with a museum collection of original remains. The cave is valuable as a natural and archaeological site in its own right.

### Do I need experience with difficult mountain hikes?

A typical visit to the main cave does not require multi-day trekking experience. Check which trail sections are accessible and their surface conditions separately; the overall tour's difficulty depends primarily on the other days in its itinerary.

## Valparaíso's naval headquarters: the former Intendancy on Sotomayor Square

**The historic naval headquarters building in Valparaíso is one of the main architectural landmarks of Sotomayor Square.** Its official historic name is *Edificio de la Intendencia de Valparaíso*, the building of the former city Intendancy. Today it houses the command of Chile's First Naval Zone (*Comandancia en Jefe de la Primera Zona Naval*).

This distinction matters: the building houses a specific regional command, not necessarily the headquarters of the country's entire navy. It stands at the end of [Sotomayor Square](/chile/place/plaza-sotomayor/) opposite the direction of the ocean. Its position and imposing facade make it immediately noticeable during a walking tour.

Our [“Hidden Treasures of Bolivia and Chile” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) includes it as an architectural stop on the Valparaíso city day. Viewing the building from the square is different from entering its working administrative premises.

## When was it built and why was it needed?

In 1906, a powerful earthquake destroyed the previous building of the city Intendancy. Construction of a replacement began in the same year and was completed in **1910**, in time for Chile's centenary celebrations. The building was designed by Chilean architect Ernesto Urquieta.

Originally, the structure served more than one organization: it housed the city's Intendancy, military administration, public services, and treasury. Upper floors were also intended as the intendant's residence and as accommodation for the president when visiting the region. For early-20th-century Valparaíso, this was a way to bring key state functions together in one prominent building beside the main square.

Its purpose later changed. The second half of the 20th century brought substantial political and administrative changes for the building. Today it is chiefly associated with the naval command and is listed among Chile's protected monuments.

## Architectural features: French influences beside the Pacific

The building is eclectic, incorporating elements of the French Renaissance and Louis XVI-era architecture. According to Chile's Council of National Monuments, the design was inspired by Paris's Hôtel de Ville, the city hall.

Notice the strict symmetry of the facade, decorative details, domed section, and clock. Together they give the impression of an official palace, very different from the more informal architecture of the port streets and colorful homes on Valparaíso's hills. For photographs, step back toward the center of the square to capture the entire building within its urban setting.

Historic descriptions also note its artificial-stone and stucco finishes, an imposing interior staircase, and furnishings brought from Paris. These are architectural facts, **not a description of rooms open to visitors on a tour today**.

The facade was restored in 2013, returning it to its former blue color. The former Intendancy was officially designated a historical monument in 1979. That same year, [Sotomayor Square](/chile/place/plaza-sotomayor/) and its surroundings received separate protection as a historic urban area.

## What can you see during a walk around the square?

The principal way for tourists to experience the building is **from the outside**. Its symmetrical composition is easy to appreciate from the square. By moving a short distance to change your viewpoint, you can notice the decoration, towers, and relationship between its facade and neighboring buildings.

The surroundings are also worth attention: the square's center holds a monument to the heroes of the naval Battle of Iquique, and Prat Pier lies toward the harbor. The building makes more sense in the context of the city's civic and maritime history. The broader history of this public space is covered on the [Sotomayor Square page](/chile/place/plaza-sotomayor/).

You can continue the walk through [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/). [Cerro Concepción](/chile/place/cerro-concepcion/) has a different cityscape, with small buildings, stairways, colorful facades, and open views of the bay. The sequence makes it possible to compare the port city's formal center with its residential neighborhoods.

## Can visitors enter the former Intendancy?

As the building is used by naval command, **free tourist entry to the interior should not be assumed**. Any opening of particular rooms for public events, tours, or special dates requires confirmation from the responsible organization. We do not automatically include an interior visit in the itinerary.

For an ordinary introduction to the site, a walk around the square, a view of the facade, and the story of the city's rebuilding after the 1906 earthquake are sufficient. The length of this stop depends on the overall Valparaíso route.

Travelers interested in urban architecture can explore our [selection of cultural and historical journeys through Chile](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/chile/). Choose a program based on its actual list of sights rather than the words “historic center” alone.

## Frequently asked questions about the naval headquarters building

### Is this an old building or a modern one?

It is historic. It was built in 1906–1910 after the previous Intendancy was destroyed by an earthquake. Its current naval function came later.

### Why does the architecture resemble a European palace?

Architect Ernesto Urquieta used French stylistic influences, including Renaissance and Louis XVI-era elements. The official monument register mentions the influence of Paris's city hall.

### Can visitors go inside?

For an ordinary visit, plan to view the exterior from [Sotomayor Square](/chile/place/plaza-sotomayor/). Interior access must be checked separately; the building's current institutional use does not make it a museum.

### When was the building designated a monument?

In 1979. It is a separate historic monument within the protected architectural ensemble of Sotomayor Square.

## Tours visiting the naval headquarters in Valparaíso

The historic building now occupied by the command of Chile's First Naval Zone stands on [Sotomayor Square](/chile/place/plaza-sotomayor/) in [Valparaíso](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/). It is commonly known as the naval headquarters or the former Intendancy. Built in 1906–1910, it occupies one of the square's principal sides and is easy to view during a walk through the port's historic center.

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} whose geographical itineraries include this historic landmark. **Its inclusion means a stop or an introduction to the architectural ensemble, not a guarantee of entry to the interior.** When choosing a route, compare how much time it allows in Valparaíso and which surrounding neighborhoods it covers.

## The Chilean coast as one day within a longer tour

On the [“VIP Chile 5*” tour](/chile/tour/chile-five-star-vip/), the Pacific coast day follows Santiago, the Atacama, and Patagonia. The itinerary ends with visits to Valparaíso and Viña del Mar. This suits travelers who want to add port history and urban architecture to their natural experiences without building the entire journey around Valparaíso.

[“Chile & Argentina Deluxe”](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-deluxe/) sets aside a separate day for Valparaíso and Viña del Mar, with a drive through the wine valleys of Curacaví and Casablanca. The itinerary also mentions Pablo Neruda's house, La Sebastiana. Here the coastal visit complements a journey that later continues through Patagonia and Argentina.

[“Hidden Treasures of Bolivia and Chile: 16 days”](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) gives the most detailed reference to this particular building. The city day lists Sotomayor Square, the naval headquarters, [Cerro Concepción](/chile/place/cerro-concepcion/), sightseeing walks, and attractions in Viña del Mar. On this journey, the port visit concludes a long itinerary through very different natural regions. Conditions for entering the building must still be distinguished from viewing its exterior.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_chili_argentina,tour_source_vip_chili_5,tour_bolivia_chile_hidden_treasures_16_days}}

## What is the building on Sotomayor Square?

The complex originally served as the residence of the regional administration. Architect Ernesto Urquieta used French historicist forms: a symmetrical facade, decorative details, and a central domed section. Today the building is a historic monument and an active naval facility. It can be viewed from the square in the context of its surrounding architecture, but a civilian tour through the offices is not part of an ordinary walking excursion.

Nearby stands the memorial to the heroes of the naval Battle of Iquique. Different stages of the port's development are visible in the historic center, from monumental administrative buildings to streets climbing the hills. That explains why the naval headquarters belongs on a Valparaíso itinerary even if only a short time is allotted to the stop.

On an independent walk, you can continue along historic streets and climb to the scenic neighborhoods of [Cerro Concepción](/chile/place/cerro-concepcion/). The resort city of [Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/) has a very different atmosphere; itineraries there often include the [Flower Clock](/chile/place/vina-flower-clock/) and walks by the ocean. These are distinct places and should not be treated as a single attraction.

## How to choose a Valparaíso itinerary

If your main goal is the architecture of Valparaíso, look at the list of walking stops and free time rather than simply whether the city is mentioned. A visit to Sotomayor Square is enough to view the headquarters facade; interior access and special naval events require separate confirmation.

For an itinerary starting in Santiago, the coast is usually visited on a day trip with an evening return. When Chile is combined with Argentina or Bolivia, the priorities change: an extra hour in Valparaíso must be balanced against onward flights, transfers, and the density of other excursion days. We can help coordinate the actual itinerary with confirmed access opportunities.

Other city-focused journeys are listed in the [Chile tours catalog](/chile/tour/) and under [“Culture and History”](/interests/culture-and-history/). To explore this particular port-city ensemble, choose a program that names the relevant stops, not just any trip passing through central Chile.

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting the naval headquarters

### Can visitors enter the building?

An ordinary sightseeing tour involves viewing the architecture from the square. Entry to the working naval facility must be arranged separately; its listing among a tour's places does not grant interior access.

### Where is the naval headquarters?

It stands opposite part of the port-side buildings on [Sotomayor Square](/chile/place/plaza-sotomayor/) in the historic center of Valparaíso. It is an easy landmark to find on a city walking tour.

### Is there an itinerary that names the building explicitly?

Yes. The [16-day Bolivia and Chile tour](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/) lists the headquarters and Sotomayor Square among the city-day sights.

### How do Valparaíso and Viña del Mar differ?

Valparaíso is known for its port history, hills, and urban architecture. Viña del Mar is another coastal city, with parks, beaches, and resort stops. They are often combined in one day, but it is best to allow time for each.
